blocks.text: Chengdu wakes up slowly, like someone who stayed out late eating hotpot. At seven-forty the sky is the colour of weak tea, the air smells of chilli oil and wet concrete, and your suitcase wheel clatters over every cracked tile between the metro exit and your new [[小区|xiǎoqū|housing compound]]. Six old brick blocks, laundry on every balcony, one ginkgo tree doing its best. At the [[大门|dàmén|main gate]], a man in a faded security jacket steps out of his booth, thermos in hand, and plants himself in your path.

blocks.e: Hold on. Who are you looking for?

blocks.text: You hold up your phone with the rental contract on it. He reads every line. He looks at you. He looks at your suitcase. He looks at you again, as if the suitcase might have a different story. Then he lifts his chin toward a little door marked [[物业|wùyè|property management]].

blocks.p: Xīn lái de? Wùyè, zài nàbiān. Ǹg.
blocks.e: New here? Property office, over there. Mm.

blocks.h: 早！吃面吗？要辣的吗？我的面巴适得很——巴适就是很好！
blocks.p: Zǎo! Chī miàn ma? Yào là de ma? Wǒ de miàn bāshì de hěn — bāshì jiù shì hěn hǎo!
blocks.e: Morning! Want noodles? Spicy? My noodles are bāshì — bāshì means really good!

blocks.text: That's from the noodle shop squeezed beside the gate, where a man in an apron waves a ladle at you through a cloud of steam. Your stomach votes yes. Your suitcase votes later. Inside the [[物业|wùyè|property management]] office, a fan creaks, a fat ledger lies open, and a woman in reading glasses is already smiling at you.

blocks.h: 你是新来的吧？这是你的钥匙。三号楼，五零一。
blocks.p: Nǐ shì xīn lái de ba? Zhè shì nǐ de yàoshi. Sān hào lóu, wǔ líng yāo.
blocks.e: You're the new one, right? Here are your keys. Building 3, flat 501.

blocks.text: The [[钥匙|yàoshi|keys]] are heavy brass on a red string. Then something odd happens. At the words "five-oh-one", her pen stops. Through the window, the guard looks up from his thermos. Nobody says anything. The fan creaks into the silence. Before you can ask, a voice like a dinner gong rolls across the courtyard, and a woman with floral oversleeves and a bag of green beans charges in, already beaming. She lives, it turns out, directly [[对门|duìmén|across the hall]] from your new flat.

blocks.h: 哎呀！你就是新来的？住五零一？对对对，就是你！
blocks.p: Āiyā! Nǐ jiù shì xīn lái de? Zhù wǔ líng yāo? Duì duì duì, jiù shì nǐ!
blocks.e: Oh my! So you're the new one? Living in 501? Yes, yes, yes, that's you!

blocks.h: 我住你对门！你吃了没有？
blocks.p: Wǒ zhù nǐ duìmén! Nǐ chī le méiyǒu?
blocks.e: I live right across from you! Have you eaten yet?

moment.prompt: Tell her you haven't eaten yet.

opts.note: 还没 (hái méi) means "not yet", the natural answer to 吃了没有, and 呢 (ne) keeps it soft and friendly.
r: 哎呀，还没吃？走走走，来我家吃！
Āiyā, hái méi chī? Zǒu zǒu zǒu, lái wǒ jiā chī!
Oh my, not yet? Come on, come on, come eat at my place!

opts.note: 没有 (méiyǒu) is understood, but 还没 (hái méi), "not yet", sounds warmer and less like you're shutting the conversation down.
r: Méiyǒu? Āiyā, nà kě bù xíng!
No? Oh dear, that won't do!

opts.note: 不 (bù) means you don't or won't eat at all; for something that hasn't happened yet, use 没 (méi): 还没吃.
r: 不吃？！你不吃饭？哎呀，难怪你这么瘦！
Bù chī?! Nǐ bù chīfàn? Āiyā, nánguài nǐ zhème shòu!
You don't EAT?! You don't eat meals? Oh my, no wonder you're so skinny!

summary: You arrive at the old Chengdu compound in the morning, get waved through by gruff guard 周大勇, are tempted by 刘志强's noodles, collect the keys to flat 501 from the property office (the clerk and guard react oddly to '501'), and meet loud neighbour 张桂芳 from across the hall, who asks if you've eaten; the electricity card is still to be sorted.
